title: The lattice sheet was the one-pass tail's buffer swap: every other frame the scene pass drew into the composer's depthless target, so the floor lattice showed through the rock; the tail no longer swaps, its gain re-priced at 0.8 ms, and the rest of the base is batched (3,711 -> 2,971 calls at 3440 wide, the picture unchanged)
context: The owner: 'go with recommendations; run the remaining base-loading steps.' The recommendations were the remaining browser steps on the branch, the owner's look at the recoloured structures, then the sheet hunt and the flags. The sheet (2026-11-06-the-weld-keeps-its-colours-and-a-clone-and-the-base-s-batching-waits-on-a-lattice-sheet) had been read as a texture-binding desync in the add stage. Branch perf-pass-2026-11-06, worktree ~/Dev/stalheart-perf; a detached worktree ~/Dev/stalheart-sheet at 6fc0ccc5 served the probes without touching the suites' tree.
outcome: THE SUITES ON THE BRANCH (before the fix, flags off): the default suite, --skip-tutorial, --pet-print and --story-world green; --colony ('Isao prints the armory') and --defense ('no unpiloted tower kill') red, and red with the same two messages on the untouched main tree e527eff4, so the base's. THE RECOLOURED STRUCTURES, LOOKED AT: on the main tree the solar complex's panels and the armory's pad draw as black cutouts (vertexColors on, no attribute); on the branch the panels are blue with orange piping and the pad shows its mechs (stills before-solar / after-solar in the session scratchpad). The greenhouse, cassettes, chips and ammo are bought prints and were not standing in any skipped sector, so they are not in the stills. THE SHEET, FOUND: a runtime hook on renderer.render for the add quad read the GL texture bindings after the draw (tDiffuse on unit 0, tBloom on unit 1, both the right textures: no desync), renderer.resetState() before the add changed nothing, the drawing buffer's alpha was 255 everywhere, and a time series of the add's output over 420 frames at one ground block showed the frame ALTERNATING, period two, between a clean value and a cyan one, on the unflagged tree exactly as on the flagged one. EffectComposer swaps its two targets after every pass whose needsSwap is true; Pass defaults it to true; the old tail swapped twice a frame (the add's ShaderPass and the OutputPass), which kept the parity; AddOutputPass, the one pass that replaced them, swapped once, so on every other frame the RenderPass drew the scene into renderTarget1, which postfx had made depthless and non-multisampled for the old tail's intermediate: no depth test, the lattice through the rock, no MSAA. The bisect of the previous entry was parity luck: a headless screenshot lands on an even or an odd frame by how many frames the boot took, and a batched tree booted one frame off from an unbatched one; 'hiding X clears it' changed the parity as much as the picture. FIXED, TEST-FIRST: test/postfx.mjs asserts new AddOutputPass().needsSwap === false (red, then green); the constructor sets it. After the fix the output no longer alternates on either tree and the flagged tree's screenshot is clean. THE TAIL RE-PRICED (headed, 3440x1353, sector 2, the same frozen scene, 7 s a mode): onePass 38.97 / 39.19 ms a frame (gpu 48.2) against separateAdd 39.88 (gpu 48.9) with the flags, 39.56 / 39.49 against 40.35 without: 0.8-0.9 ms a frame, not the 1.9 of the previous entry, whose extra was the skipped MSAA and depth on the odd frames; the pixel comparison holds (no channel over 1/255, 25,564 and 21,289 of 13.96M differing by 1). THE BASE BATCHED: batch: true on the six domes, the four bridges, hugin, stalheart, rotor, radar, the launcher (keep LAUNCH_SLED, CLAMP_L, CLAMP_R), the four rockets and the two wrecks (24 of 34 base-layout structures and all ten dome-city ones; not the SH02, the salvage, the foundry, the bays, the garage, the pearls, each for the reason in the previous entry). Measured against the same tree without the flags: at 3440x1353 draw calls 3,711 -> 2,971 a frame (chain off 1,869 -> 1,499), frame 39.5 -> 39.0 ms and gpu 48.2 -> 48.2 (noise); at 1440x900 1,944 -> 1,410 calls (the base 1,232 / 308 objects -> 696 / 174), cpuFrame 10.7 -> 10.0 ms, gpu 21.7 -> 22.0 (noise), 0 meshes with vertexColors and no colour attribute on either. So the batching is a fifth fewer draw calls and a little CPU, no GPU time at this scene: the chain's cost at the owner's width is pass A's vertex work (the lattice's 2.3M triangles drawn twice), not the draws. Stills with the flags on (the Stalheart rig, the dome city with its bridges, the Hugin pad, the radar) look as before.
alternatives: Keeping the composer swapping and giving renderTarget1 a depth buffer and samples: a second multisampled full-size target for nothing; the last pass has no reason to swap.
Dropping the one-pass tail for its 0.8 ms: kept; it is output-identical and the probe's 'separateAdd' split still holds the old tail for A/B.
Batching only where it paid in GPU time: nothing did; the flags are on for the draw calls and the CPU, which cost nothing to look at.
Trusting single headless screenshots for a render bisect again: no; the next render bisect samples the drawing buffer over a run of frames (the probe's time series) before it hides anything.
evidence: Suites on the branch at 6fc0ccc5 (flags off): default exit 0, skip-tutorial 0, pet-print 0, story-world 0, colony 1 (Isao prints the armory), defense 1 (no unpiloted tower kill); the main tree e527eff4 run the same way: colony 1, defense 1, the same two messages.

Stills (session scratchpad perf/): before-solar.png black panels and pad, after-solar.png blue panels, orange piping, the mechs on the pad; flags-stalheart, flags-dome-w, flags-hugin, flags-radar, flags-bridge-w1 with every flag on.

The add's bindings after its draw (SH-dump2): unit 0 tDiffuse (EffectComposer.rt1 / rt2 on alternate frames), unit 1 tBloom, the program's samplers 0 and 1. SH-reset (resetState before the add): the sheet. SH-read: alpha 255 over the ground block. SH-time-sheet / SH-time-perf: the 48x48 block's mean at (0.5, 0.15) alternating [6.9, 62.9, 71.5] / [6.8, 12.9, 17.8] every frame on both trees. SH-fixed-sheet / SH-fixed-perf after the fix: [6.8, 12.9, 17.9] on every sampled frame, the flagged screenshot clean.

vendor/EffectComposer.js:128 `if ( pass.needsSwap )`, vendor/Pass.js:18 `this.needsSwap = true`; src/postfx.js makes finalComposer.renderTarget1 samples 0 and depthBuffer false and renderTarget2 samples 4.

R-3440-perf (flags, fixed): baseline 24.3 fps 41.67 ms gpu 54.0 calls 2,971; onePass 25.7 fps 38.97 ms gpu 48.19; separateAdd 25.1 fps 39.88 ms gpu 48.89; onePassAgain 25.5 fps 39.19 ms gpu 48.43; chain off 50 fps 20.02 ms gpu 14.35 calls 1,499; PIXDIFF oldVsNew max 1 differing 25,564 over1 0, oldVsOld 0. R-3440-sheet (no flags, fixed): baseline 24.6 fps 40.69 ms gpu 51.4 calls 3,711; onePass 25.3 fps 39.56 ms gpu 48.2; separateAdd 24.8 fps 40.35 ms gpu 48.94; onePassAgain 25.3 fps 39.49 ms gpu 48.43; chain off 50 fps 20.03 ms gpu 14.41 calls 1,869; PIXDIFF max 1 differing 21,289.

R-1440-perf (flags): 50 fps 20.01 ms gpu 22.0 calls 1,410 tris 3.33M cpuFrame 10.02; chain off gpu 7.82 calls 800; Story base 696 calls / 174 objects. R-1440-sheet (no flags): gpu 21.71 calls 1,944 cpuFrame 10.69; chain off gpu 7.82 calls 1,068; Story base 1,232 / 308. vertexColors without a colour attribute: 0 on both.
